# Physics Anchor: Large Metal-Cluster Matter-Wave Interference

Primary source: <https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09917-9>

## Grounded Summary

The reported experiment extends matter-wave interference to large sodium nanoparticles:

- material class: metal clusters
- object scale: more than 7,000 atoms
- mass: greater than 170,000 Da
- reported macroscopicity: `mu = 15.5`
- method class: matter-wave interferometry using optical gratings
- evidence class: interference fringes consistent with quantum propagation

## What This Supports

This supports the claim that quantum interference can be observed in objects substantially larger and more complex than small molecules or single atoms.

It also supports a useful engineering direction: matter-wave interferometry is a sensitive platform where control schedules, decoherence models, phase selection, and analysis methods matter.

## What This Does Not Support By Itself

This paper does not by itself prove:

- a consciousness effect,
- brain-to-quantum-state projection,
- biological control of wavefunction collapse,
- or a special role for organoids or BCI streams.

Q-PRISM treats those as hypotheses to test through controlled experiments.
